neighboring_unit_entries.title: A weighted GCD quadratic form supplies an essentially optimal resonator
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Theorem 2 allows optimized positive coefficients rather than uniform weights, situates the form in the GCD-sum hierarchy, and explains that nearly extremal square-free sets are enough to produce an essentially optimal resonating Dirichlet polynomial even without identifying an exact extremizer.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Prime-local weights factor the GCD objective into an Euler product
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The proof chooses a controlled band of primes, defines a multiplicative function on square-free integers, rewrites the weighted GCD form into divisor sums, and factorizes the normalized quantity into local prime contributions; two lemmas then isolate size and truncation obligations.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The authors predict that the same resonance design varies continuously across 1/2<σ<1, but the structural variable is the smoothness of the integers in the resonator. As σ decreases, an essentially optimal support is expected to use a different prime profile.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The introduction states a large-value result for ζ(σ+it) with a constant ν_σ and gives endpoint asymptotics as σ approaches 1 and 1/2. It describes this as a smooth transition between known endpoint regimes and says the proof, including the changing smoothness of resonator integers, will appear in a forthcoming publication.
directed.conceptual_reading: Method transfer is expressed as a change in representation capacity: the prime-factor profile that makes a resonator efficient depends on the vertical line. The endpoint interpolation is a prediction about optimal design, not a theorem proved in this span.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is the same resonance ratio with a σ-dependent multiplicative support, whose smoothness profile tunes the available gain.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The proof is explicitly deferred. Exact ν_σ formulas and endpoint constants are extraction-sensitive, so this unit supports strategic perspective rather than local verification.
directed.uncertainty: Low uncertainty that the claim is deferred; high uncertainty about its quantitative formula and sharpness.

supported: The source announces a large-value result for zeta(sigma+it) throughout 1/2<sigma<1, defines a constant nu_sigma, and states endpoint asymptotics for that constant.
It describes the result as a smooth transition between endpoint regimes.

It explicitly says the proof will appear in a forthcoming publication and reports that the proof shows a nontrivial decrease in the smoothness of integers in an essentially optimal resonator as sigma decreases.
inference: Reading the changing prime-factor profile as sigma-dependent resonator design is well supported by the stated smoothness claim.
The announced endpoint behavior supplies a strategic interpolation picture, but this unit does not locally prove it.
unsupported_or_imported: The spontaneous claim that the resonance design itself 'varies continuously' is stronger than the source, which calls the resulting estimates a smooth transition but only says resonator smoothness decreases in an interesting and nontrivial way.
Calling the endpoint interpolation merely a 'prediction' misstates its status: the authors announce a precise result and defer its proof, rather than present it as a conjecture.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: 'Representation capacity' and 'prime profile' are useful abstractions but should remain explicitly interpretive.
context_or_ocr_risk: The formula for nu_sigma and both endpoint asymptotics are layout-sensitive, and no proof appears in this unit.
Sharpness near one is discussed through consistency with an external conjecture, not established here.
revision_instructions: Replace 'varies continuously' with the source-safe statement that the method gives an announced smooth transition in the lower-bound constants and that resonator smoothness changes nontrivially with sigma.
Label the quantitative extension as an announced result whose proof is deferred, not as a prediction; reserve conjectural language for the sharpness discussion attributed to Lamzouri's conjecture.

section_entries.label: Construction and proof of the large GCD sum
section_entries.mathematical_role: Builds multiplicative weights on square-free numbers, evaluates their Euler product, and constructs a divisor-closed truncation retaining the required weighted mass.

unit_result_entry.title: Occupancy caps compress an infinite multiplicative support to at most N integers
unit_result_entry.why_material: Primes are partitioned into scale blocks, numbers with excessive occupancy in any block are removed, and factorial/binomial estimates show that the remaining square-free support is divisor closed and has cardinality at most N.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: The block definition, occupancy threshold, divisor closure, and entropy-style cardinality estimate form one compression mechanism.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: Block endpoints, occupancy thresholds, floors, products, and binomial estimates are extraction-sensitive; exact inequalities and exponents require the PDF.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Taking logarithms turns the Euler product gain into a prime-density integral
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Small local weights permit logarithmic linearization of the Euler product, and a prime-number-theorem approximation converts the accumulated gain over the chosen prime band into the target iterated-logarithm exponent.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: An exponential tilt proves the discarded multiplicative mass is negligible
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: A union bound reduces discarded mass to blockwise tails; inserting a tilt b>1, factorizing over primes, and balancing its gain against the occupancy penalty yields a negative exponent and proves the truncation preserves the Euler-product main term.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Prime-local weights create Euler-product gain, while blockwise occupancy caps and exponential tilting compress the infinite support without losing the mass that drives the extremal form.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The paper constructs a nearly maximal family rather than characterizing an actual extremizer.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Near extremality by local design plus global compression

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: An infinite multiplicative support is compressed by capping how many primes a number may take from each scale block. The remaining square-free family is automatically divisor closed, and factorial/binomial estimates show its combinatorial entropy stays below log N.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The primes are partitioned into blocks P_k. Sets M_k contain numbers whose occupancy in block P_k exceeds a threshold, and M is the support of f with all such sets removed. Thus each element of M is square-free with bounded block occupancy, and M is divisor closed. Stirling-type factorial bounds, binomial estimates, and prime counts bound the product of blockwise choices and give |M|≤N for sufficiently large N.
directed.conceptual_reading: Block occupancy is a coarse sufficient statistic for support size. Capping it preserves downward divisibility while turning a multiplicative family into a product of finite combinatorial choices that can be entropy-bounded.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is prime-scale partition → occupancy vector → removal of overloaded blocks → divisor-closed support → product of binomial counts → cardinality bound.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Block endpoints, thresholds, floors, and binomial exponents are extraction-sensitive. The unit proves capacity control, not preservation of weighted mass; that is a separate lemma.
directed.uncertainty: Low uncertainty about the compression mechanism; high uncertainty about exact thresholds and inequalities.

supported: The proof partitions the finite prime set into blocks P_k and removes numbers exceeding a prescribed occupancy threshold in any block.
The remaining square-free set M is explicitly divisor closed.
Factorial estimates, binomial bounds, and prime counts bound the product of blockwise choices and yield |M|<=N for sufficiently large N.
inference: Block occupancy is a useful coarse statistic for cardinality, and its downward stability explains why the cap preserves divisor closure.
Viewing the final product of binomial counts as an entropy bound is a sound conceptual paraphrase.
unsupported_or_imported: The spontaneous reading calls the original multiplicative support infinite, but the chosen prime band P is finite and a square-free function supported only on P has a finite, though potentially enormous, support.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: 'Combinatorial entropy stays below log N' summarizes the exponential counting estimate rather than quoting a formal entropy calculation.
context_or_ocr_risk: Block endpoints, occupancy thresholds, floors, factorial inequalities, and binomial exponents are extraction-sensitive.
This unit proves cardinality control only; preservation of the weighted mass is handled separately.
revision_instructions: Replace 'infinite multiplicative support' with 'large finite multiplicative support' or simply 'the full square-free multiplicative support generated by the finite prime band'.
